content: {"summary":"To verify whether PostgreSQL is still presenting the old certificate, compare the serial (or end‑date) of the certificate returned by the server with the one on disk using openssl. If they differ, reload PostgreSQL (SELECT pg_reload_conf() or systemctl reload) so it picks up the new files. The replica (auth‑db‑02) has its own certificate and timer and must be reloaded in the same way.","likely_cause":"PostgreSQL was not reloaded after the certificate files were renewed, so it continued serving the previous (expired) certificate.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Compare server‑presented certificate with the file on disk using openssl; differing serials indicate the server is still using the old cert","evidence_ids":["RB-024#2"],"quote":"Different serials mean the server is still on the old certificate."},{"text":"Reload PostgreSQL configuration (SELECT pg_reload_conf() or systemctl reload) to make it load the new certificate without a full restart","evidence_ids":["RB-024#2"],"quote":"Reload, don't restart: SELECT pg_reload_conf();"},{"text":"The replica auth‑db‑02 has its own certificate and its own renewal timer, so it must also be reloaded after a renewal","evidence_ids":["RB-024#3"],"quote":"Yes. auth-db-02 has its own certificate and its own timer."},{"text":"In the April 2025 incident the timer wrote a new cert but PostgreSQL was not told to load it, causing the old cert to be served until a manual reload fixed it","evidence_ids":["RB-024#4"],"quote":"The timer had written a valid replacement on 2025-03-09, but nothing told Postgres to load it."}],"next_checks":["Run the openssl s_client command against auth-db-01 and compare its serial to /etc/postgresql/16/main/server.crt","Verify the systemd timer pg-cert-renew.timer ran and wrote new files on both primary and replica","Confirm that pg_reload_conf() (or systemctl reload) was executed after the timer wrote new certs","Check that auth-db-02’s certificate files were updated and reloaded in the same way as the primary"]}
